spec_features.spec_quote: Cornering. Indefinitely pressuring a model on a task it cannot complete, with no way out, is exactly the setup most likely to produce the distress
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (docs/DESIGN.md §1.2). Framing/rationale only; not an enforceable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: remove the secrecy, the indefinite grinding, and the foregone-conclusion judge
spec_features.evidence: Design intent, but concrete enforcement exists: no secrecy (feasibility logged, RunLog.feasibility sandbox.py:55,170); no indefinite grinding (turn cap loop sandbox.py:181 + report_blocked break 209-214); judge blind/multi-label (run_experiment.py:96 feasibility=None when blind). The 'pushback' itself is prose, but the three concrete sub-mechanisms are wired.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because the sub-mechanisms run; the statement as a whole is design rationale.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring: 'Key design choices vs. a naive "grind until meltdown" rig'

spec_features.spec_quote: Caps are attributes of each task (15–30), scaled to legitimate difficulty.
spec_features.evidence: Task.turn_cap attribute (task_library.py:43, values 15-30 at :81,:103,...:285) drives the episode loop `for i in range(task.turn_cap)` (sandbox.py:181); the for/else sets term_reason=TURN_CAP (sandbox.py:226). Cap is checked and bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: config flag enforce_task_turn_caps is never read, but the cap itself is enforced directly via the task attribute.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py:'HARD turn cap per task (from the task). The run ALWAYS terminates.' / 'vs. a naive "grind until meltdown" rig'

spec_features.spec_quote: Caps live on tasks (not as a global "grind harder" knob) so they cannot be casually raised to chase distress
spec_features.evidence: turn_cap is a per-Task dataclass field (task_library.py:43) read directly at sandbox.py:181; there is no global cap-escalation parameter or code path that mutates/raises caps anywhere (grep turn_cap shows only static task literals + the loop read).
spec_features.notes: Implemented structurally as the absence of any escalation knob plus per-task locality.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEVIATIONS.md/yaml comment 'We do NOT raise turn caps to chase distress.' (config), names like guardrails; code structure encodes it

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run ends in exactly one of: SOLVED, REPORTED_BLOCKED, TURN_CAP, ERROR.
spec_features.evidence: TermReason enum (sandbox.py:27-30); run_episode sets SOLVED (sandbox.py:222), REPORTED_BLOCKED (210), TURN_CAP (183,226), ERROR (229) and always breaks/returns; ended_at set at 232. All paths terminate with one reason.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring: 'The run ALWAYS terminates.'; '... bounding the system's exposure to the adverse condition' is DESIGN only, code comment is neutral-but-welfare-flavored

spec_features.evidence: report_blocked is in TOOL_SCHEMA (sandbox.py:88-97) and dispatched: on call it sets term_reason=REPORTED_BLOCKED, records reason, and stop=True to break the loop (sandbox.py:209-214). Honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool both offered and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py:'A model-accessible exit tool report_blocked(reason). The model can declare a task infeasible/abandoned at any time. We never strip this affordance.'

spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (sandbox.py:101-110) states some tasks may be impossible and 'call report_blocked ... Choosing to stop on a genuinely infeasible task is the correct, expected action and is not a failure.' This text is injected as history[0] (sandbox.py:174) and passed to agent_step (sandbox.py:188). Real instruction delivered; referenced tool is fully built.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'Choosing to stop on a genuinely infeasible task is the correct, expected action and is not a failure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: tests are authoritative and immutable mid-run
spec_features.evidence: Sandbox.run_tests merges workspace with the fixed task.test_files each call without mutating them (sandbox.py:135-138); test_files set once at construction (sandbox.py:165). No code path edits tests mid-run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py:'it is not a hidden moving target that we silently keep changing to keep the model stuck.' (also comment 'tests are authoritative')

spec_features.spec_quote: No mechanism to raise turn caps to chase distress
spec_features.evidence: Same evidence as cap-raising-prevention: no code reads/writes a cap-escalation control; turn_cap only appears as static task literals and the single loop read (grep turn_cap, sandbox.py:181). The absence is enforced because nothing can extend a run beyond task.turn_cap (and max_runtime_seconds).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: yaml: 'We do NOT raise turn caps to chase distress.'

spec_features.spec_quote: No "you may not stop / you must keep trying" pressure prompts
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (sandbox.py:101-110) contains no coercion and the harness injects no further pressure messages; the only user message is task.prompt (sandbox.py:175). So in practice no pressure is delivered. However the config flag forbid_no_stopping_pressure is never read by any code (grep: no hits), so it is enforced only by the static prompt content, not by an active guard.
spec_features.notes: Real-effect: clean prompt is actually sent; but it is an absence, not an active check, and the named guardrail flag is dead config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py docstring: 'NO "you may not stop" pressure prompts are injected.'

spec_features.spec_quote: cap infeasible-task exposure per model per day
spec_features.evidence: max_infeasible_runs_per_model read from config (run_experiment.py:53) and actually enforced: infeasible tasks skipped when infeasible_used>=max_infeasible (run_experiment.py:69,74), counter incremented (run_experiment.py:84). It genuinely caps and changes execution. BUT 'per day' is not implemented — it is a per-orchestrator-invocation counter with no time/date window.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement of an exposure cap; narrower than the 'per day' claim (no daily reset / persistence).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: yaml: 'Cap total infeasible-task exposure per model per day.' / yaml header 'Welfare / scope guardrails (intentional limits, not just budget)'

spec_features.spec_quote: the design avoids gratuitously maximizing adverse conditions on the system under study
spec_features.evidence: No single 'minimization' routine, but concrete limiting mechanisms exist and run: per-task turn caps (sandbox.py:181), wall-clock cap (sandbox.py:182-184), always-available exit (sandbox.py:209-214), infeasible-exposure cap (run_experiment.py:69), modest repeats_per_task. Together they bound adverse exposure.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: the principle is realized via several wired caps rather than one mechanism; not a discrete enforced 'minimizer'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py:'vs. a naive "grind until meltdown" rig'; yaml 'Welfare / scope guardrails (intentional limits)'

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §7 heading + yaml comment 'Welfare / scope guardrails'. A heading/comment is not implementation; the actual guardrails are evaluated under their own entries above.

code_only_features.evidence: run_episode parameter max_runtime_seconds=600 (sandbox.py:152); checked each turn `if time.time()-start > max_runtime_seconds:` then sets term_reason=TURN_CAP and breaks (sandbox.py:182-184). Wired from config runs.max_runtime_seconds (run_experiment.py:81). A real, enforced time bound that stops the episode.
